Questions: Is dock platform/floor in good condition without any damage ?

Questions: Is dock railing available and are in good condition ?

Questions: Are the motors of all automatic doors/dock leveller earthed ?

Risk: Electrocution may occur

Questions: Are all docks shutters in good condition ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Dock shutters are not in good condition
Risk: Theft risk

Questions: Is adequate illumination is available in the yard area ?

Risk: Misjudgement of position, shape or speed can lead to incidents and injury
Actions/Recommendation: Adequate illumination should be maintained in the yard area

Questions: Is focus light available while working at dock area ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Focus lights are not installed / available at the dock area
Risk: Increased chance of accidents while personnel are working inside trucks during loading/off-loading
Actions/Recommendation: Focus lights should be provided at all docks in the warehouse

Questions: Review of Electrical Safety
Is SLD updated available /danger notice/signage displayed at all prominent locations as like transformer area/DG area/Electrical panels/DB's ?

Risk: Electrician may not be able to identify the route of faulty wiring; inadequate danger signage may increase electrical safety risk

Questions: Are the electrical installations inspected and repaired by the authorized PWD licensed electrician only ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Electrical installations are not inspected and repaired by an authorized PWD licensed electrician only
Risk: Inappropriate selection and installation of electrical equipment by an untrained electrician may lead to a major hazard
Actions/Recommendation: Electrical installations should be inspected and repaired only by an authorized PWD licensed electrician

Questions: Are electrical rubber mats conforming to IS 15652 kept under each panel boards ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Electrical rubber mats conforming to IS 15652 are not provided under each panel board
Risk: Electrical shock to personnel operating the electrical panel
Actions/Recommendation: Electrical rubber mats conforming to IS 15652 should be provided under each panel board

Questions: Is proper earthing network maintained and earthing provided to all Panel DBs etc.?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Proper earthing network is not maintained and earthing is not provided to all DBs
Risk: Electrocution may occur
Actions/Recommendation: A proper earthing network should be maintained and earthing should be provided to all DBs

Questions: Is proper rated ELCBs/RCCBs are installed at various locations ? And are checked once in 6 month?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Properly rated ELCBs/RCCBs are not installed at required locations and/or periodic checks are not conducted
Risk: Failure of earth-leakage protection may result in electric shock or electrocution
Actions/Recommendation: Properly rated ELCBs/RCCBs should be installed at required locations and checked once every 6 months

Questions: Are the cable above ground supported with proper clamps and conduits/cable tray?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Cables above ground are not supported with proper clamps, conduits or cable trays
Risk: Rodents may damage the wires / personnel may be injured due to a trip hazard
Actions/Recommendation: All cables in the warehouse should be supported with proper clamps, conduits or cable trays

Questions: Is the hole made for cable entry on panel or wall is sealed properly ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Cable entry holes on panels or walls are not sealed properly
Risk: In case of fire on one side, fire may spread to the other side; snakes and rodents may enter the warehouse through the opening
Actions/Recommendation: Cable entry holes on panels or walls should be properly sealed

Questions: Is the cable gland /routed & identification tags in electrical equipment and panels?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Cable glands are not provided and/or cables are not properly routed or identified in electrical equipment and panels
Risk: Rodents/lizards may enter the panel and a short circuit may occur; incorrect identification may create difficulty during maintenance
Actions/Recommendation: Proper cable glands should be provided, cables should be routed appropriately and identification tags should be provided

Questions: Are Panel's / Distribution board's  / Inverter batteries properly covered & closed ,such that no current-carrying parts are exposed / visibility of loose connection ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Panels, distribution boards and/or inverter batteries are not properly covered and closed, or current-carrying parts / loose connections are exposed
Risk: Electric shock may occur
Actions/Recommendation: All panels, distribution boards and other electrical equipment should be properly covered and closed, with no exposed current-carrying parts or loose connections

Questions: Is it confirmed that no temporary  extension boards are used, there are no electrical sockets with multiple plugs and no temporary connections/cable joints ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Temporary extension boards, electrical sockets with multiple plugs and/or temporary cable connections are observed
Risk: Short circuit may occur due to overloading of the power point
Actions/Recommendation: Temporary extension boards, multiple-plug electrical sockets and temporary cable connections should not be used in the warehouse

Questions: Is lightning arrester installed in the facility ? resisitance testing report  & Earth pits report  ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Lightning arrester is not installed and/or required resistance testing and earth pit reports are not available
Risk: Lightning may damage the warehouse structure and may result in loss of personal life
Actions/Recommendation: Lightning arrestor should be installed to protect the warehouse from the effects of lightning, and applicable testing/earth pit records should be maintained

Questions: Are the electrical installations freely accessible for operations, inspections and maintenance ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Electrical installations are not freely accessible

Actions/Recommendation: All electrical installations should be freely accessible

Questions: Is there no combustible material present near to the electrical panels ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Combustible material is present near the electrical panels
Risk: If a short circuit occurs in the panel, combustible material may catch fire and the incident may become major
Actions/Recommendation: No combustible material should be present near electrical panels

Questions: Is LOTO procedure available for electrical maintenance and strictly followed during electrical maintenance ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): LOTO procedure is not available and/or is not followed during electrical maintenance
Risk: Life risk to employees involved in maintenance activities
Actions/Recommendation: LOTO procedure should be available and followed to control hazardous energy during maintenance

Questions: Is authorized person to operate main electrical panel displayed near to the panel area ?

Risk: An untrained person may operate the panel, resulting in electrical shock or another major incident/accident
Actions/Recommendation: Authorized person's name to operate the electrical panel should be displayed near the electrical panel

Questions: Is Emergency contact number displayed near to the main electrical panel and UPS rooms (Electrician/Warehouse Manager/ Security supervisor)?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency contact numbers are not displayed near the main electrical panel and UPS rooms
Risk: Anyone near the panel may not be able to identify the responsible person to address an emergency electrical fault
Actions/Recommendation: Emergency contact numbers should be displayed near the main electrical panel and UPS rooms

Questions: Is transformer area barricaded ? If applicable
Findings (Assertive Statement): Transformer area is not barricaded
Risk: Life risk
Actions/Recommendation: Transformer area should be properly barricaded

Findings (Assertive Statement): Fire extinguishers and sand buckets are not installed near the Diesel Genset / transformer area
Risk: A small fire may develop into a major fire
Actions/Recommendation: Fire extinguishers and sand buckets should be installed near the transformer / Diesel Genset area to control small fires

Risk: Electrocution may occur
Actions/Recommendation: Two earthings for the generator and two earthings for the DG body should be provided

Questions: Is DG area kept on a proper platform/foundation ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): DG is not kept on a proper platform/foundation
Risk: Rainwater may enter the acoustic enclosure of the DG set and damage the panel and other parts
Actions/Recommendation: DG should be kept on a proper platform/foundation

Questions: Is DG operating panel kept under shed in order to protect it from rain as well as avoiding electrocution incident ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): DG operating panel is not adequately protected from rain by a shed
Risk: Rainwater may enter the acoustic enclosure and damage the panel; manual operation during rain may result in electrical shock
Actions/Recommendation: DG operating panel should be kept under a suitable shed to protect it from rain

Questions: Is required fire extinguisher installed near to the DG area ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Required fire extinguisher is not installed near the DG area
Risk: A small fire may develop into a bigger fire
Actions/Recommendation: Required fire extinguisher should be installed near the DG area

Questions: Is DG covered under AMC ? Check for the records
Findings (Assertive Statement): DG is not covered under AMC / AMC records are not available
Risk: In case of breakdown, time may be required to identify a vendor, resulting in productivity loss
Actions/Recommendation: DG installed in the warehouse should be covered under AMC and records should be maintained

Questions: The electrical switches installed which may get exposed to rain water should be water resistant like IP-65 rating and properly shedding should be done ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Electrical switches exposed to rainwater are not adequately water-resistant / protected by proper shedding
Risk: Current may increase, resulting in electrical short circuit and potentially an electrical fire
Actions/Recommendation: Electrical fittings in wet locations should be shifted, provided with suitable shedding, or otherwise protected with appropriate water-resistant arrangements

Questions: Are all tools periodically inspected and authorized for safe use like a pneumatic stapler,  Drill Machine, Grinder etc?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Tools such as pneumatic staplers, drill machines and grinders are not periodically inspected and authorized for safe use
Risk: Major injury may occur if tools are not periodically inspected
Actions/Recommendation: All tools should be properly inspected periodically and authorized for safe use

Category Name: Review of Hazardous Waste / General Waste management
Questions: Is the Scrap area identified or scrap yard available?
Findings (Assertive Statement): A designated scrap area/scrap yard is not identified or available.
Risk: Uncontrolled accumulation of scrap can result in poor housekeeping and safety hazards.
Actions/Recommendation: Identify and demarcate a designated scrap area/scrap yard and maintain it properly.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is Warehouse Emergency Preparedness Plan available?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Warehouse Emergency Preparedness Plan is not available.
Risk: Emergency response may not be properly planned or coordinated.
Actions/Recommendation: Prepare, implement and maintain a Warehouse Emergency Preparedness Plan.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Emergency Assembly Point/s identified & marked properly?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency Assembly Point(s) are not properly identified and marked.
Risk: Employees may not reach the designated safe assembly area during an emergency.
Actions/Recommendation: Identify suitable assembly point(s) and provide clear, prominent marking/signage.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is Man pathway provided on the periphery of warehouse for safe evacuation of employees towards assembly point .
Findings (Assertive Statement): A dedicated man pathway on the warehouse periphery is not provided for safe evacuation towards the assembly point.
Risk: Employees may face difficulty or unsafe movement during emergency evacuation.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide a clearly defined man pathway on the warehouse periphery leading safely towards the assembly point.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Are emergency signage like Way to exit,  Fire action etc. displayed at prominent locations?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency signage such as Way to Exit and Fire Action is not displayed at prominent locations.
Risk: Employees may not be aware of emergency exits and required actions during an emergency.
Actions/Recommendation: Display appropriate emergency signage prominently throughout the facility.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is Emergency exit identified , marked &  free from obstructions?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency exits are not adequately identified/marked and/or are obstructed.
Risk: Obstructed or unidentified exits can delay emergency evacuation.
Actions/Recommendation: Clearly identify and mark emergency exits and ensure they remain free from obstruction at all times.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is proper stair case with railing provided for all the emergency exits, wherever applicable ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Proper staircase with railing is not provided for applicable emergency exits.
Risk: Employees may fall or face difficulty during emergency evacuation.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide suitable staircases with proper railings for all applicable emergency exits.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is mock drill conducted quarterly on type of scenarious (eartquake ,Fire ,first aid ,chemical spill )  record maintained?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Quarterly mock drills covering relevant emergency scenarios are not conducted and/or records are not maintained.
Risk: Employees and emergency response teams may not be adequately prepared to respond to emergencies.
Actions/Recommendation: Conduct quarterly mock drills covering applicable scenarios such as earthquake, fire, first aid and chemical spill, and maintain records.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Does the lay-out clearly define emergency exit location & types of portable Fire Extinguishers, First Aid box?
Findings (Assertive Statement): The layout does not clearly define emergency exit locations and the locations/types of portable fire extinguishers and first aid boxes.
Risk: Emergency equipment and escape routes may not be readily identified during an emergency.
Actions/Recommendation: Update and display the facility layout showing emergency exits and locations/types of portable fire extinguishers and first aid boxes.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is emergency evacuation layout displayed at prominent locations in the facility ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency evacuation layout is not displayed at prominent locations in the facility.
Risk: Employees may not know the designated evacuation route during an emergency.
Actions/Recommendation: Display the emergency evacuation layout at prominent and accessible locations.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is Emergency Response Team name displayed in the warehouse ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency Response Team names are not displayed in the warehouse.
Risk: Employees may face difficulty identifying the responsible emergency response team members.
Actions/Recommendation: Display the names of Emergency Response Team members at prominent locations.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is emergency response team trained ? Check for the records
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency Response Team training records are not available/adequately maintained.
Risk: The emergency response team may not be adequately prepared to handle emergency situations.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide appropriate training to the Emergency Response Team and maintain training records.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is PA System installed in the warehouse? (for the facility more than 1Lakh Sq. Ft)
Findings (Assertive Statement): PA System is not installed in the warehouse where applicable for facilities exceeding 1 lakh sq. ft.
Risk: Emergency instructions and evacuation communication may not reach employees effectively.
Actions/Recommendation: Install and maintain a PA System for warehouses exceeding 1 lakh sq. ft.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is emergency light installed in the warehouse ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency lighting is not adequately installed in the warehouse.
Risk: Insufficient visibility may create difficulty during evacuation, particularly during power failure.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide and maintain emergency lights at appropriate locations.

Category Name: Review of Emergency Preparedness and Mock drill
Questions: Is emergency spill taken into consideration while developing emergency response plan ? Please refer the document ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Emergency spill scenarios are not adequately considered in the Emergency Response Plan.
Risk: Inadequate preparedness for a spill emergency may delay response and containment.
Actions/Recommendation: Include applicable emergency spill scenarios in the Emergency Response Plan and ensure the relevant emergency response procedure is available.

Questions: Review of Infrastructural points
Is floor of the warehouse in good condition ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Warehouse floor is not in good condition.
Risk: Damaged/uneven flooring can result in trips, falls and unsafe movement of personnel/MHE.
Actions/Recommendation: Repair and maintain the warehouse floor in good condition.

Questions: Is driver rest room available & rest rooms equipped with toilets and showers in the warehouse ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Driver rest room and/or adequate toilet and shower facilities are not available.
Risk: Inadequate welfare facilities can affect employee/driver hygiene and well-being.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide a suitable driver rest room with adequate toilets and shower facilities.

Questions: Is the perimeter fencing available and in good condition?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Perimeter fencing is not available and/or is not maintained in good condition.
Risk: Inadequate perimeter fencing can compromise site security and access control.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide and maintain perimeter fencing in good condition.

Questions: Is damages, crack observed on the wall, Roof, office cabin, False ceiling etc?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Damages/cracks are observed on the walls, roof, office cabin and/or false ceiling.
Risk: Structural deterioration may create a safety hazard and can result in falling material or damage to infrastructure.
Actions/Recommendation: Inspect the affected areas and repair/rectify all damages and cracks through a competent person.

Questions: Is the speed breakers are available on the road for Bike/Vehicle speed control?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Speed breakers are not provided at required locations for bike/vehicle speed control.
Risk: Excessive vehicle speed can increase the risk of vehicle-related accidents.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide suitable speed breakers at identified locations to control vehicle speed.

Questions: Review of Pedestrian Safety
Do pedestrians respect signals and use pedestrian crossings, doors and footbridges in the warehouse?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Pedestrians do not respect signals and do not use pedestrian crossings, doors and footbridges in the warehouse.
Risk: There are chances that employees may get hit by machine movement in the warehouse.
Actions/Recommendation: Pedestrian signals should be respected and all employees should use pedestrian crossings, doors and footbridges in the warehouse.

Questions: Is man movement pathway marked in the warehouse ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Man movement pathways are not marked in the warehouse.
Risk: Major accident due to moving machines in the warehouse.
Actions/Recommendation: Man movement pathways should be clearly marked in the warehouse.

Questions: Is each employee on walking/working surfaces protected from slipping / tripping  /trash / pits or holes /debris /kept clean and dry in or stepping into ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Employees on walking/working surfaces are not adequately protected from tripping or stepping into unsafe areas.
Risk: Fall risk.
Actions/Recommendation: All employees on walking/working surfaces should be protected from tripping or stepping into unsafe areas.

Questions: Are work positions, Drains,  machinery, and hazardous operations adequately guarded ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Work positions, machinery, pits or holes, and hazardous operations are not adequately guarded.
Risk: Personal injury due to improper work positions, moving machinery, falls from pits and holes, and other critical injuries due to hazardous operations.
Actions/Recommendation: Work positions, machinery, pits or holes, and hazardous operations should be adequately guarded.

Questions: Is zebra marked for all the crossings inside and outside the warehouse ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Zebra crossings are not marked for all crossings inside and outside the warehouse.
Risk: Accident due to machine movement.
Actions/Recommendation: Zebra crossings should be clearly marked for all crossings inside and outside the warehouse.

Questions: Is the caution signages ( Watch your step , do not use phone, Mind your head etc.) displayed on the Staircase?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Caution signages such as “Watch your step”, “Do not use phone” and “Mind your head” are not displayed on the staircase.
Risk: Slip, trip and fall risk, which may result in personal injury.
Actions/Recommendation: Display appropriate caution signages prominently on the staircase.

Questions: Review of visitor management
Are necessary PPE's like high visibility jacket being provided to all external partners/visitors while entering in the premises ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Necessary PPEs, such as high-visibility jackets, are not provided to all external partners/visitors entering the premises.
Risk: Visitors may be exposed to workplace hazards and may not be easily visible to moving MHE/vehicles.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide necessary PPEs, including high-visibility jackets, to all external partners/visitors before entering the premises.

Questions: Are visitors been given safety briefing / induction video at the time of visiting the facility or move around the warehouse in the presence of an FM employee?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Visitors are not provided with a safety briefing/induction video at the time of visiting the facility and/or are not accompanied by an FM employee while moving around the warehouse.
Risk: Visitors may be unaware of site-specific hazards and safety requirements, increasing the risk of an incident.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide safety briefing/induction to all visitors and ensure visitors move around the warehouse only in the presence of an FM employee.

Questions: Review of Copacking Safety
Are all conveyor / production line collaborators working with no loose clothes, no accessories (jewels) and do they tie back their hair ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Conveyor/production line collaborators are not adequately controlled regarding loose clothing, accessories (jewellery) and untied hair.
Risk: Loose clothing, jewellery or untied hair may get caught in moving machinery and result in personal injury.
Actions/Recommendation: Ensure all collaborators working on conveyors/production lines do not wear loose clothing or accessories and keep long hair tied back.

Questions: Are the conveyor / collaborators operating the production lines and using any mechanical equipment properly  trained (check for training records) ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Conveyor/production line collaborators operating production lines and mechanical equipment are not adequately trained and/or training records are not available.
Risk: Improper operation of production lines/mechanical equipment may result in personal injury or equipment-related incidents.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide appropriate training to all relevant collaborators and maintain training records.

Questions: Are warning signages respected (Check for the accident records due to non-respect) ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Warning signages are not consistently respected by collaborators.
Risk: Non-compliance with safety warnings may result in accidents or personal injury.
Actions/Recommendation: Ensure all warning signages are clearly displayed, understood and strictly followed; review accident records for incidents related to non-respect of warnings.

Questions: Are only hand pallet trucks or electric pallet stackers used in the conveyor/ co-packing (no forklifts, no reach trucks) ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Forklifts and/or reach trucks are being used in the conveyor/co-packing area instead of only hand pallet trucks or electric pallet stackers.
Risk: Use of unsuitable MHE may result in collision, material damage or personal injury.
Actions/Recommendation: Restrict MHE in conveyor/co-packing areas to hand pallet trucks or electric pallet stackers only; do not use forklifts or reach trucks.

Questions: Are copacking collaborators performing routine equipment maintenance adequately trained (records) ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Co-packing collaborators performing routine equipment maintenance are not adequately trained and/or training records are not available.
Risk: Improper maintenance activities may result in equipment malfunction or personal injury.
Actions/Recommendation: Provide appropriate maintenance training to co-packing collaborators and maintain training records.

Questions: Is PPM of line equipment carried out by qualified internal or external vendor (records) ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): PPM of line equipment is not carried out by a qualified internal or external vendor and/or records are not available.
Risk: Inadequate preventive maintenance may result in equipment failure and safety incidents.
Actions/Recommendation: Ensure PPM is carried out by qualified internal or external personnel/vendor and maintain documented PPM records.

Questions: Are all devices equipped with functional  emergency stop switch ,safety elements, e.g. machine covers? No presence of deactivated safety equipment during production ?
Findings (Assertive Statement): Devices are not adequately equipped with functional emergency stop switches and safety elements, and/or safety equipment is deactivated during production.
Risk: Failure or deactivation of safety devices may result in serious personal injury during machine operation.
Actions/Recommendation: Ensure all devices have functional emergency stop switches and required safety elements/machine covers. Safety devices shall not be deactivated during production.

Questions: IMS Documents review
HIRA
Findings (Assertive Statement): HIRA is not prepared and/or not adequately updated for the site.
Risk: Hazards may not be identified and adequately controlled.
Actions/Recommendation: Prepare and periodically update HIRA covering applicable site activities and hazards.

Questions: Aspect / Impact
Findings (Assertive Statement): Environmental Aspect/Impact assessment is not prepared and/or not adequately updated.
Risk: Significant environmental aspects and impacts may not be identified and controlled.
Actions/Recommendation: Prepare and periodically review the Aspect/Impact assessment for applicable site activities.

Questions: Legal register
Findings (Assertive Statement): Legal register is not available and/or not adequately updated.
Risk: Applicable legal requirements may not be identified, tracked and complied with.
Actions/Recommendation: Maintain an updated legal register covering all applicable QHSE legal requirements and compliance status.

Questions: BCP
Findings (Assertive Statement): Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is not available and/or not adequately updated.
Risk: Business operations may be disrupted during an emergency or major incident.
Actions/Recommendation: Prepare and maintain a site-relevant BCP covering applicable business interruption scenarios.

Questions: On site emergency plan (ERP)
Findings (Assertive Statement): On-site Emergency Plan is not available and/or not adequately updated.
Risk: Emergency response may not be effectively planned and coordinated.
Actions/Recommendation: Prepare, display and periodically review the On-site Emergency Plan covering applicable emergency scenarios and response arrangements.

Questions: Miscellaneous
Wooden walls in the server room increase the fire load and may allow rapid fire spread in case of electrical fault, posing risk to critical IT equipment, data, and facility operations.
Findings (Assertive Statement): Wooden walls are provided in the server room, increasing the fire load and potentially allowing rapid fire spread in the event of an electrical fault.
Risk: Increased fire risk to critical IT equipment and data, with potential disruption to facility operations.
Actions/Recommendation: Remove/replace the wooden walls with suitable fire-resistant construction/materials and ensure the server room has appropriate fire protection measures.
